findings.title: Non-positive `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s` degrades dispatches silently instead of failing fast
findings.description: Description: `int` coercion in `squadron/config/manager.py` (`_coerce_value`) accepts `0` and negative values for `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s`, and `_background_idle_timeout_s()` forwards the value verbatim into `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` in `_read_turn()`. With `delay <= 0`, `asyncio.timeout` fires immediately, so the first waiting read of a dispatch that tracked a background agent goes straight into `_stop_background()`: the agent is stopped and the dispatch returns partial text with a WARNING that reads "no activity for 0s" (or a negative number) — a confusing signal for a misconfiguration, and the run's output silently degrades. This conflicts with the fail-fast rule (invalid state should be caught at the boundary). Suggest rejecting non-positive values where the key is read (raise `ValueError` with the key named, matching `get_typed_config`'s existing mismatch errors) or validating range in `_coerce_value` for this key.

findings.title: No load-tier test for the new background-wait / idle-timeout dispatch path
findings.description: Description: This slice adds concurrency-layer behavior to `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch()` (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py`): multi-turn `receive_response()` reads, a per-message idle timer, `stop_task` fan-out, and cross-turn text joining, all driven from `squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py`. The project's Python testing rules require at least one load test for slices touching concurrency paths, asserting latency/resource bounds under a realistic configuration, and CI already gates `tests/load/` via plain `pytest` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `uv run pytest`; `testpaths = ["tests"]`). The new timing tests in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py` use a 0.05s timer and one or two scripted agents — unit-scale. A load test (e.g., many simultaneous tracked agents, repeated idle-timeout cycles, realistic timer values) asserting bounded wall-clock time and no event-loop starvation would close the gap the rules name for exactly this class of change.

findings.title: `background_tasks_waited` metadata key reports agents seen, not agents actually waited on
findings.description: Description: `self.background_tasks_waited = turns.ledger.seen_count` counts every distinct waited-type agent tracked during the dispatch, even when it started and finished inside the same turn so the dispatch never actually entered the waiting state (`turns.waiting` was never true). The name (used in `ActionResult.metadata` in `src/squadron/pipeline/actions/dispatch.py` and asserted in `tests/pipeline/actions/test_dispatch_session.py`) implies "waited for". Consider renaming to `background_tasks_seen`/`_tracked` or documenting the looser semantic on the dataclass field, so a reader of run metadata doesn't infer a wait that didn't happen.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` has grown past the project's ~300-line file guidance
findings.description: Description: After this change the file is roughly 480 lines, with `SDKExecutionSession` now covering connect/disconnect lifecycle, the multi-turn dispatch protocol, background-task stopping, idle-timeout policy reads, reconnect/seeding, and settings introspection. The pure turn bookkeeping was correctly extracted to `squadron/pipeline/sdk_turns.py`; the remaining growth is mostly the dispatch-reading loop and its retry/timeout wrappers. AGENTS.md targets ~300 lines "where practical" — extracting the read/retry/timer loop (e.g., a `_TurnReader` collaborator) would keep the class describable in one clause and make the idle-timeout semantics directly testable without a session. Not blocking; flagging the trend.

findings.title: `scripted_session()` returning `object` forces pervasive `type: ignore` in the new tests
findings.description: Description: `tests/pipeline/conftest.py` defines `scripted_session(client) -> object`, which makes every use site in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py`, `test_executor_each.py`, `test_summary.py`, and `test_compact.py` carry `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` / `[arg-type]` comments (dozens). Since the function always constructs a real `SDKExecutionSession`, annotating it with that type (it's already imported inside the function) would remove the ignores and keep the shared fixture honest for whatever tooling covers tests later (pyright currently excludes `tests` per the documented issue #50, but the fixture is also consumed by the `typed_config`-style strictness the new tests otherwise model).

findings.title: Core new behavior verified: turn joining, leftover discard, idle-stop, settings policy, bool config round-trip
findings.description: Description: I traced the new paths against the real code rather than the diff alone and they hold: (1) `seed_context` now frames exactly once (`frame_summary_for_seed` only in `_seeded_options`; the doubled framing in `SummaryAction._execute_restore` was removed and guarded by `test_restore_frames_summary_exactly_once`); (2) the D6 discard path clears `parts` while preserving the ledger, so a leftover injected result cannot mask our own result or leak foreign prose; (3) stream-end with tracked agents raises `ProviderError` (fail-closed) while stream-end with nothing tracked preserves today's behavior; (4) `unusable_reason` latches after a failed reconnect and is enforced by `_require_usable()` on `dispatch`/`compact`/`seed_context`, with later `each` items flagged and `query()` never reached (verified in `TestUnusableSessionInBatch`); (5) the per-path settings policy table in `tests/providers/sdk/test_settings_policy.py` matches the actual builders (review templates all set `[project]`, PR override `[]`, audit hardcodes `[project]`, summary/PR composer `[]`), and `get_typed_config`'s bool check correctly precedes the int check (`bool` is an `int` subclass); (6) `load`/`save` of bool config round-trips native TOML booleans and hand-written non-bool TOML fails loudly with the key named. No silent-failure paths found in the new I/O code: stop-task failures log at ERROR with `exc_info`, idle timeouts and discarded turns log at WARNING, and reconnect failures log at ERROR plus latch.
